questions.prompt: AP Classes (Current): Name a current AP course.
questions.sourceNote: Prepared for 12 Oct 2026. Curated recall rarity for a general trivia audience, calibrated to 786 imported Krillion answers: 10=7.5%, 15=1.3%, 30=23.0%, 60=31.4%, 85=34.9%, 100=1.9%. These are comparison proportions, not measured player probabilities or forced per-question quotas. The 15-point QUIRKY tier is reserved for deceptively obvious answers. Complete 42-course College Board catalogue as checked on 12 Oct 2026, including Business with Personal Finance and Cybersecurity. Course pages linked by the catalogue establish subject content; https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/courses/ap-business-personal-finance and https://apstudents.collegeboard.org/courses/ap-cybersecurity confirm the newer subjects. AP prefixes optional. Broad groupers follow least-rare ownership: English/Lang → English Language; Literature/Lit → English Literature; History → United States History; Calculus/Calc → Calculus AB; Physics → Physics 1; Physics C → Mechanics; Computer Science/CS → Computer Science A; Economics/Econ → Macroeconomics; Government/Gov → US Government; Spanish → Spanish Language; Art/Studio Art → Drawing. Distinguishing course qualifiers retain independent catches. No retired Physics B or Computer Science AB.

questions.prompt: Chess Terminology: Name a chess piece, move, tactic, position, or rule.
questions.sourceNote: Prepared for 12 Oct 2026. Curated recall rarity for a general trivia audience, calibrated to 786 imported Krillion answers: 10=7.5%, 15=1.3%, 30=23.0%, 60=31.4%, 85=34.9%, 100=1.9%. These are comparison proportions, not measured player probabilities or forced per-question quotas. The 15-point QUIRKY tier is reserved for deceptively obvious answers. Broad bank of standard chess vocabulary, including tournament/time-control terms and named tactical or mating patterns; excludes named openings, players, fictional characters, engines, and variant names. Rules: https://handbook.fide.com/chapter/E012023 ; tactics and endgames: https://lichess.org/practice and https://lichess.org/training/themes ; definitions also checked across the linked Chess.com glossary entries. En passant is the 15-point QUIRKY exception because it is the familiar internet-meme answer that feels more obscure than it is. Pawn, bishop, rook and check own their plain-word aliases; specialized patterns require qualifiers. Knight accepts Horse; Rook accepts Castle, whereas Castling is a separate move. Named problem themes Grimshaw and Novotny are retained as obscure tactics, not openings. Composition themes verified against https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimshaw_(chess) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novotny_(chess) .

These are comparison proportions, not measured player probabilities or forced per-question quotas. The 15-point QUIRKY tier is reserved for deceptively obvious answers. Finite set of 14 standardized external connector families and physically distinct SuperSpeed variants, including historical/obsolete types and AB receptacles. Excludes speed standards alone, USB Power Delivery modes, internal motherboard headers, proprietary connectors, Lightning and Thunderbolt branding. USB 2/3 Standard-A share one family because the outer mating form is compatible; enlarged SuperSpeed B/Micro variants remain distinct. Bare Mini USB maps to Mini-B (30), Micro USB to Micro-B (30), Type B to Standard-B (30). Sources: https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/CabConn_Legacy_3_1_Compliance_Rev_1_1.pdf establishes SuperSpeed A/B, Powered-B and Micro-A/B/AB; https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/documents/usb_otg_and_eh_3-0_release_1_1_10may2012.pdf establishes Micro-AB OTG; https://www.usb.org/usb-type-c establishes Type-C. USB-IF compliance updates establish withdrawn Mini-A/Mini-AB.

questions.prompt: Famous Physicists: Name a real physicist, including historical natural philosophers and astrophysicists.
questions.sourceNote: Prepared for 12 Oct 2026. Curated recall rarity for a general trivia audience, calibrated to 786 imported Krillion answers: 10=7.5%, 15=1.3%, 30=23.0%, 60=31.4%, 85=34.9%, 100=1.9%. These are comparison proportions, not measured player probabilities or forced per-question quotas. The 15-point QUIRKY tier is reserved for deceptively obvious answers. Broad historical bank covering Nobel laureates, classical physics, experimental physics, mathematical physics and astrophysics; not a claim to list every physicist. Nobel membership and award years were checked against the Nobel Foundation API. Non-Nobel scientists and blurbs use the University of St Andrews MacTutor biographies at https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/ and AIP Physics History Network https://history.aip.org/acapsearch/ ; Examples checked include https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Noether_Emmy/ , https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Bassi/ , https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Hawking/ and https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Faraday/ . Engineers such as Tesla qualify through substantial physical research; generic inventors and fictional scientists are excluded. Surname aliases are unique except documented familiar owners: Curie → Marie, Bohr → Niels, Thomson → J. J., Bragg → William Lawrence (same tier as William Henry). Related scientists remain separate full-name catches. Ambiguous partial inputs may still prompt an autocorrect suggestion, which requires confirmation.

questions.prompt: Name a real-life language that uses a non-Latin writing system.
questions.sourceNote: Prepared for 12 Oct 2026. Curated recall rarity for a general trivia audience, calibrated to 786 imported Krillion answers: 10=7.5%, 15=1.3%, 30=23.0%, 60=31.4%, 85=34.9%, 100=1.9%. These are comparison proportions, not measured player probabilities or forced per-question quotas. The 15-point QUIRKY tier is reserved for deceptively obvious answers. Broad bank of living, classical and liturgical languages with an established non-Latin writing tradition. Latin romanization does not disqualify a language. Includes established alternate scripts (for example Punjabi and Malay), but excludes invented one-off transcriptions and constructed languages. Primary script-language mappings checked against Unicode CLDR; additional script histories and names checked in https://omniglot.com/writing/langalph.htm ; source indexes are recorded in research-sources.json. Common language umbrellas group varieties as one catch: Chinese includes Mandarin and Cantonese; Persian includes Farsi, Dari and Tajik; Kurdish includes Sorani; Mongolian includes its traditional and Cyrillic writing. Script names themselves are not answers: Arabic and Hebrew are accepted because they are also language names. This is a broad curated bank, not an exhaustive global inventory.

Exact finite set of all 46 visible labels in the user-supplied diagram, saved alongside this pack as landforms-reference.png. Includes water bodies, ice features, and biomes because the user explicitly selected this diagram; not restricted to geomorphological landforms. No unlabelled additions such as Estuary or Continent. Additional product references: https://x.ai/grok , https://stability.ai/stable-diffusion , https://www.midjourney.com/ and https://www.perplexity.ai/ .
